messages:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a quiet bench overnight to compare SmoothQuant (act-aware) vs AWQ vs GPTQ on longspan workloads (32k/64k/128k). putting raw results here so ops/devex can look at deploy implications.
aj: saved the artifacts to s3: s3://redwood-exps/quiet-bench/2103456789/ — includes perf traces + evals.json
felix: nice. what's the model and quant knobs?
maya: model: rdw-unicorn-7b (fp32 baseline). quant configs: AWQ-4/8, GPTQ-4/8, SQ-actaware-int8, SQ-actaware-fp8-mix. batch sizes: 1,4,8. kv cache lengths: native up to 128k. ctx tested: 32k, 64k, 128k.
sam: short summary numbers? p95 latency and quality delta vs fp32?
maya: summary from eval-bot below (raw numbers later). key takeaways: 1) SQ-actaware-int8 keeps quality within 0.7% BLEU-equivalent delta at 64k vs fp32 but p95 jumps ~18% vs fp32 when batch=1. 2) SQ-fp8-mix keeps quality within 0.2% and p95 close to fp32 (+4%). 3) AWQ shows larger regressions on instruction-following tasks at long ctx (1.5-2.2% delta) but is cheaper. 4) GPTQ was unstable at 128k (KV eviction thrash) — saw some token repetitions in regen.
eval-bot: EVAL SUMMARY: model=rdw-unicorn-7b | ctx=[32k,64k,128k] | metrics={qual_delta_fp32:[0.2,0.7,1.8], p95_ms:[+4%,+18%,+45%] for SQ-int8(b1)} | full JSON at s3.
aj: can you paste the command you ran? want to reproduce on dedicated pool.
maya: sure, used the bench harness:```./run_bakeoff.sh --model rdw-unicorn-7b --quant-configs sq-actaware-int8,sq-fp8mix,awq,gptq --ctx 32k,64k,128k --batches 1,4,8 --save-trace s3://redwood-exps/quiet-bench/2103456789/```
felix: noted the p95 delta for SQ-int8 at batch=1 — probably due to extra dequant ops + activation reshuffle on the critical path. did you try kernel fusion flags?
maya: yes tried fusion=on/off. fusion helped p95 ~6-8% for 64k but made memory fallback worse at 128k.
sam: deployment notes? for Dedicated vs Hosted: does any quant config require special runtime flags?
maya: SQ-fp8-mix needs the new FP8 path (runtime flag: --enable-fp8-mix) and updated kernel set (v2.3). AWQ/GPTQ work on current kernels but AWQ benefits from continuous batching >=4. SQ-int8 requires act-aware preproc step at quant time (calibration traces) — added ~2h quant-time for 7B.
ej: (typo, meant aj) ops question: can Dedicated pools enforce the fp8 flag automatically per route?
aj: yes, Console rollout supports per-model runtime flags; we can pin fp8-mix only to dedicated nodes with v2.3 kernelset. will add a rollout plan.
maya: one more weirdness: at 128k with GPTQ we saw KV cache eviction oscillation when batching>1, leading to regen duplicates. trace:```TRACE: kv_eviction: idx=34901 evict->refill=0.52s loop_count=18```
felix: sounds like our eviction heuristics don't handle large per-request KV churn when quantized weights change memory footprint. we should add a per-model kv-evict-safety factor for quantized variants.
sam: action items?
maya: 1) aj to draft rollout gating: allow SQ-fp8-mix only on v2.3 dedicated pools + smoke test. 2) felix to add kv-evict-safety param and rerun GPTQ 128k. 3) maya to produce a short doc (2p) describing quality vs latency tradeoff matrix and cost estimates. 4) ops to provision one small dedicated fp8 pool for canary.
aj: putting a ticket in infra board now: INFRA-2191. tagging @eng-platform for rollout hook. :thumbsup:
felix: I'll try kv-evict-safety=1.2 and run quick smoke on 128k. if stable, we can push a fallback policy that routes to SQ-fp8-mix when eviction freq > threshold.
eval-bot: REGRESSION ALERT: GPTQ-128k-batch>1 triggered regen-dup metric >0.05 on 12/18 tests. See s3 logs.
maya: thanks — i'll write the 2p and link in the ticket. quick note for the customer profile doc: recommend fp8-mix for latency-sensitive read-heavy workloads; SQ-int8 for cost-first but expect p95 hit at small batch/low concurrency.
sam: perfect. let's sync tomorrow 10am to align on rollout windows.
maya: SG.
aj: ack.
felix: will update when kv change lands.
